slides.title: 4 facts that sound made up
slides.body:
Guess each one before you swipe.
Keep score. No peeking!

slides.title: A day on Venus is longer than its year.
slides.body: True or false? Make your guess, then swipe.

slides.title: Venus spins very slowly
slides.body: One spin on its axis takes about 243 Earth days, but one trip around the Sun takes only about 225. It also spins the opposite way to most planets.

slides.title: You can see the Great Wall of China from the Moon.
slides.body: True or false? (With your own eyes, no telescope.)

slides.title: A popular myth
slides.body: The wall is very long but very narrow. From the Moon, about 384,000 km away, no single human-made structure can be seen with the naked eye. Astronauts have confirmed it.

slides.title: The world's largest desert is the Sahara.
slides.body: True or false? Think carefully about what makes a desert.

slides.title: It's Antarctica
slides.body: A desert is defined by how little rain or snow falls, not by heat. Antarctica gets so little that it counts as the largest desert on Earth, bigger than the Sahara.

slides.title: Saturn would float in water.
slides.body: True or false? (If you could find a big enough bath.)

slides.title: Lighter than it looks
slides.body: Saturn is made mostly of hydrogen and helium, and its average density is lower than water's. It's the only planet in our solar system like that.

slides.title: How many did you get right?
slides.body: Comment your score out of 4. And save this to test a friend later.
